title: LLM Vocabulary Response (JSON, Record)
description: Response containing the model's vocabulary tokens
documentation:
## Purpose
Returns the full token vocabulary of a loaded LLM, enabling token-level analysis, prompt engineering tools, and custom tokenization utilities to operate without a separate tokenizer library.

## When to use
This is the response to a `get_vocab` request in a [LLM Generation Request](https://capdag.com/browse/media:llm-generation-request;json;record). Use it when you need to enumerate, inspect, or count the tokens the model recognises.

## Notes
The `vocab` array is ordered by token ID. The `vocab_size` field should equal the length of `vocab`; include it as a convenience for consumers that only need the count without iterating the full array. Vocabulary extraction is typically slow on large models; cache the result when possible.

## Data format
The serialization format of structured data. A value tagged with both a data-format
and a structure tag tells consumers exactly how to parse the bytes into a structured
representation. JSON is the default for cap inter-step data exchange.

JavaScript Object Notation. Text-based, human-readable, ubiquitous. The default
serialization for structured cap inputs and outputs.

## Record marker
Presence marker indicating the value's content is a key-value mapping at its
root: a JSON object, a CSV row with named columns, a TOML table, an INI file.
Independent of `list-marker` — a value can be both (a list of records),
either alone, or neither.

The value's content is a key-value mapping. Consumers can expect to address
fields by name.
